extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, institutional research administrators, grant applicants, and others who follow NIH grants policy and process updates
extracted.subtask_description: A news/updates page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource changes that affect grant applicants and awardees. Meant to alert readers to new formats, initiatives, review-process changes, and resources they should follow when preparing applications or managing awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select models appropriate to research questions (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize scientific soundness, human relevance, and translational potential when choosing models; select the approach that best answers the research question rather than adopting a method for its novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format has been issued based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable NIH submissions, follow the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified in that format (watch for detailed instructions in the linked resource).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic — NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances a commitment to replication and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should address replication and reproducibility considerations in applications and awards to strengthen reliability; NIH’s Replication and Reproducibility Initiative aims to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize these efforts across the enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format and expect possible linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH released a 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PF5 application format described by NIH and plan for administrative outcomes such as splitting into linked awards post-review; consult the overview resource to understand key features and formatting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes after the lapse in appropriations, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that strong applications can fall below the 33% discussion cut-off and be scored as 'competitive but not discussed'; understand how this designation arose and what it means for your application status and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized peer review (CSR) consolidation effects
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR); updates summarize one year of consolidation and its initial effects on peer-review efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that centralization may change review workflows, timelines, and how study sections are organized; consider implications for submission timing and expectations about review processes.
